title: Structure of the Earth and Geologic Time

standard_code: JSS 3 Intermediate Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: The Earth has layers (crust, mantle, outer core, inner core) studied using seismic waves; the geologic time scale; relative and absolute (radiometric) dating of rocks and fossils. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 3, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free JSS 3 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): the Earth's layers, seismic evidence, dating rocks, the geologic time scale and the fossil record. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.
key_sub: Lower rock layers are usually older.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth has a thin solid crust, a thick hot mantle, a liquid outer core and a solid inner core. Scientists learned this from seismic waves: S-waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core.

The geologic time scale divides the Earth's 4.6-billion-year history into eons, eras and periods. Relative dating uses the order of rock layers and fossils; absolute dating uses the half-lives of radioactive isotopes to give ages in years.

Example

Which layer is liquid?

S-waves do not pass

Answer: the outer core

Example

Half-life 5,730 years; 1/4 left. Age?

Two half-lives

Answer: 11,460 years

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the mantle is liquid lava.
  • Thinking relative dating gives an age in years.
  • Thinking humans lived with dinosaurs.

faq.a: From how seismic waves travel and bend through different layers.
A fossil of a species that lived for a short time over a wide area, used to date rock layers.

items.q: Which process turns loose sediment into sedimentary rock?
items.e: Minerals cement the grains together.

items.q: What are the three main types of rock?
items.e: The rock cycle links them.

items.q: Which best describes Earth's lithosphere?
c: solid iron and nickel under enormous pressure
thin, rocky outer layer; thickest under continents
rigid outer layer of crust and uppermost mantle, broken into plates
thick layer of hot solid rock that moves by slow convection
items.e: Match the layer.

items.q: Which statement about the age of oceanic crust is correct?
c: it is the same age everywhere
it is youngest at mid-ocean ridges and gets older away from them
it is older than most continental crust
it is oldest at mid-ocean ridges
items.e: Oceanic crust is rarely older than about 200 million years.

items.q: What does radiometric dating measure?
c: the ratio of a radioactive parent isotope to its daughter isotope, to find an absolute age
the order of rock layers only
items.e: Uranium–lead dating is used for zircons.

items.q: Which best describes Earth's asthenosphere?

items.q: Evidence: P waves speed up again in the inner core. What does it show?

The asthenosphere is hot and partly soft.
items.e: We learn about the interior mainly from seismic waves and density.

items.q: What is a mineral?
c: a naturally occurring inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and crystal structure
a substance made by living things
items.e: Quartz is SiO₂.

items.q: How does an igneous rock form?

items.e: Granite and basalt are igneous.

items.q: A rock has uranium-235 and lead-207 in a ratio of 1 : 3 (half-life of uranium-235: 704 million years). How old is it? (Assume all the lead-207 came from decay.)
items.e: 1 : 3 means 1/4 is left → 2 half-lives = 1,408 million years.

items.q: A rock has uranium-235 and lead-207 in a ratio of 1 : 63 (half-life of uranium-235: 704 million years). How old is it? (Assume all the lead-207 came from decay.)

items.q: About how old is Earth?

items.q: A rock started with 32 g of parent isotope and no daughter. After 3 half-lives, how much daughter isotope is there?
items.e: Daughter = original − parent left = 32 − 4 = 28 g.

items.q: Halima compares a shark fin and a dolphin flipper. They do the same job. Does this show a close evolutionary relationship?

items.e: Analogous structures do not show close ancestry.
